analysis.investment_thesis: ARE&M offers the most reasonable Magic Formula entry point of this group — earnings yield of ~11.3% (EBIT INR 1,622 Cr / EV ~INR 14,354 Cr) is just below my 12% threshold, and ROCE of 16.2% is decent but not exceptional. The ongoing capex supercycle for EV/energy storage is compressing near-term FCF to nearly zero, making this a 'show-me' story on whether new capacity translates to higher ROIC.
key_strengths: Earnings yield ~11.3% (EBIT/EV) is borderline attractive — closest to Magic Formula territory in this cohort
Near-zero net debt (D/E 0.04; borrowings INR 310 Cr vs equity INR 7,737 Cr) gives financial flexibility for the energy transition capex
Revenue CAGR 11.2% and net profit CAGR 11.8% over 6 years show consistent compounding in core lead-acid business
key_risks: FCF collapsed to INR 159 Cr in FY25 despite INR 1,351 Cr OCF — capex of INR 1,200 Cr is consuming nearly all cash generation
ROCE of 16.2% is acceptable but not a wide-moat business; operating margins are thin at 6.36% (EBITDA margin ~13%)
Technology disruption risk: if lithium/new-chemistry batteries commoditize faster than anticipated, returns on new capex may disappoint
red_flags: CWIP surged to INR 1,201 Cr (FY25) from INR 641 Cr (FY24) — heavy capital commitment with unproven returns in new energy
Finance costs rising at 35.8% CAGR (6Y), signaling debt creep as capex cycle expands
Other Income jumped to INR 222 Cr in FY25 (from ~INR 100 Cr range) — partly flattering headline PAT
analysis.detailed_analysis:
ARE&M is the only stock in this set where the Magic Formula inputs are close to attractive. EBIT/EV at ~11.3% is just below my 12% floor, and ROCE of 16.2% (capital employed ~INR 7,998 Cr) is workable if sustained. The lead-acid business is mature and cash-generative, funding the EV/lithium bet. The balance sheet is pristine (D/E 0.04), and five consecutive years of positive OCF give credibility to the earnings quality.

The key issue for Greenblatt's framework is that the capex cycle is destroying near-term FCF — INR 1,200 Cr capex against INR 1,351 Cr OCF leaves almost nothing for shareholders in FY25. CWIP at INR 1,201 Cr is committed spending that has yet to generate EBIT. If the new energy investments earn ROIC above 20%, the stock becomes genuinely interesting; if returns revert to the current 16%, a HOLD is the right call. At EV/EBITDA of ~10.5x, there is some margin of safety, but not enough to call a buy.
